methods.notes: Legacy ID retained. The intended baseline is the complete final Sun Stage 2 (BERT-TextCNN plus CoreNLP/Tregex/Tsurgeon phrase extraction). method_conformance_status was flipped to 'verified_method_level_independent_reconstruction' by explicit user authorization on 2026-08-04 (B0-R2 gate, recorded in EXPERIMENT_EVENTS.jsonl): the component-vs-method cross-walk is documented in docs/B0_R2_METHOD_CROSSWALK.md (Tsurgeon is an honest non-implementation with a fail-closed guard; lexicon scale and segmentation mechanisms are disclosed adaptations). formal_status was flipped to 'ready' and command_status to 'formal_ready_candidate_authorized' by explicit user authorization on 2026-08-10 (B0-R4 formal candidate closure: Gold-blind candidate run bound to formal input v2, F1 0.71865 identical to the B0-R3 snapshot, double-run semantically byte-identical; authorization dry-run package outputs/reports/sun_rule_only_method_gate_authorization_dry_run.json). The runner remains a development reconstruction and must not be reported as Sun's original implementation or an exact reproduction; the formal candidate result is NOT yet a published formal result and final experiment readiness additionally requires the other two methods.

The development runner now requires and SHA-binds a persisted B0 artifact, applies only Gold-blind field-level repair plans, records accepted/rejected patches, and retains B0 atomically on rejection. Formal use remains blocked until the complete B0 and trigger budget are locked. A real run additionally requires explicit --allow-llm authorization. As of 2026-08-08 (supervisor decision, MASTER_PIPELINE.md §8.8.1) this method is DOWNGRADED to a comparison-only arm and will not be pursued further: the full 150-call run (commit 74614e3) was net-negative on the primary metric (coarse F1 0.7621 vs Rules-Only 0.7986) because the trigger+repair recipe added false positives (actor P 0.7077->0.2754) instead of recall.

Replaces the whole Stage 2 without running the Sun pipeline or reading Gold. It must use the same frozen inputs, output contract, evaluator, and Stage 3 as the other two methods. Real calls require explicit authorization.
